subject: Evaluation checkpoints, commercial slab structure and renewal uplift
messages:
From: Anika Rao <anika@levelup.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@levelup.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot & MAP - proposed checkpoints and commercial ask

Hi Marissa / Connor,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We want to formalize a short MAP so our procurement team can sign off. High level ask: a 6-week evaluation with two checkpoints that, if met, trigger a staged commit and a performance-based discount.

Attached: initial MAP outline (LevelUp-MAP-v2.pdf). Procurement asked for a simple slab or tiered pricing tied to throughput after week 4. Also flag: on renewals, our finance lead (Michael) will push for step-down credits unless we get documented uplift commitments.

Can you share:
- A clean MAP with milestone acceptance criteria (week 2, week 4)
- Pricing slab that maps to committed TPS and token volumes
- Preliminary renewal uplift framework (how do we document expansion incentives vs. step-down)

Best,
Anika
Procurement Lead | LevelUp AI

Attachments: LevelUp-MAP-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 124 KB)

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Rao <anika@levelup.ai>, procurement@levelup.ai
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot & MAP - proposed checkpoints and commercial ask

Hi Anika — appreciate the clear ask and the call yesterday. I've sketched a MAP and commercial slab we think balances risk and runway. See attached: LevelUp-MAP-v3.pdf and a draft SOW. Key points below.

MAP (6 weeks) — acceptance criteria:
- Week 2: Integration & baseline run (success = SDK integration + <50ms p50 on 512-token payloads for 1k/min bursts)
- Week 4: Scale validation (success = sustained throughput at agreed TPS target for 48 hours with error rate <0.5%)
- Week 6: Business validation (success = qualitative sign-off on output quality from 2 product owners + token-cost within projected envelope)

Commercial slab (provisional):
- Tier A (pilot commit): 3-month reserved baseline -> 50% of expected peak TPS @ 10% discount vs on-demand
- Tier B (ramp commit): 6-12 month commit for 100% peak TPS @ 20% discount + 10% additional volume credit after hitting month 2 targets
- Failure to meet Week 4 acceptance: default to on-demand billing for incremental throughput until rebenchmarked

Renewal / uplift notes (preliminary):
- For first renewal, we propose a documented uplift path: if LevelUp increases committed TPS by >=25% within first 9 months, Redwood will provide a one-time credit equal to 5% of trailing 3-month usage to offset migration friction.
- If usage declines >30% vs committed baseline at renewal, standard step-down windows apply but we can negotiate a grace rebenchmark period (30 days) if product changes are in flight.

Next steps:
1) Prune the acceptance criteria to procurement's format (we can convert to a checklist).
2) Confirm which slab you prefer (A vs B) so we can put numbers into an SOW.
3) Connor will own technical validation scheduling.

I've attached the MAP (v3) and a lightweight SOW draft. If these look good I'll loop in legal for a short commercial term sheet.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0123

Attachments: LevelUp-MAP-v3.pdf (application/pdf, 210 KB); SOW-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 48 KB)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Anika Rao <anika@levelup.ai>
Cc: procurement@levelup.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot & MAP - proposed checkpoints and commercial ask

Thanks Marissa — quick commercial clarification and two options to present to LevelUp procurement.

Option 1 (Conservative):
- Pilot: 3-month soft-commit (month-to-month with 30% uplift holdback)
- Ramp: 6 month firm-commit with 15% volume discount once ramp target met
- Renewal uplift: standard tiered credits (3% / 5% / 7% depending on 12/18/24 month extend)

Option 2 (Incentivized):
- Pilot: 6-week evaluation with a conditional credit if both wk2 & wk4 pass (credit = one month of reserved capacity at 75% of pilot rate)
- Ramp: 12-month commit @ 20% discount plus a 5% re-commit credit if usage grows >=25% in first 9 months
- Renewal uplift: bespoke uplift guarantee — if LevelUp scales >=40% year-over-year, Redwood will tier discounts on new incremental volume (5% then 3% on next slabs)

Operational asks for procurement table:
- Clear acceptance checklist (Marissa to provide formatted checklist)
- Named SLAs for Week 4 throughput tests and remediation windows
- Legal to confirm minimal termination language for pilot vs commit

Connor — can you confirm the runbook and whether we can guarantee the Week 4 48-hour sustained throughput test in our hosted region? I want to be comfortable with the Incentivized option before putting the 12-month pricing on paper.

Priyom Das
Senior Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

---

From: Anika Rao <anika@levelup.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@levelup.ai>, procurement@levelup.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot & MAP - proposed checkpoints and commercial ask

Marissa / Priyom — thanks, both options look sensible. Procurement prefers Option 2 (Incentivized) but we need a clean table to present to finance showing: starting committed TPS, discount tiers, what triggers the one-time pilot credit, and the exact renewal uplift language. Michael flagged that any renewal uplift guarantee must be unilateral (i.e., documented in the contract) rather than informal.

Can Redwood legal draft a short commercial term sheet that includes:
- The Week 2, Week 4, Week 6 acceptance checklist (point-form)
- Option 2 pricing slab numbers (we can insert numeric TPS after the next call)
- Renewal uplift clause: "If Customer increases committed capacity by >=25% within first 9 months from effective date, Vendor will apply a one-time credit equal to 5% of trailing 3-month usage applied at renewal."

If you can get that to us by next Wednesday (11/03), procurement will fast-track. Also happy to do a short 30-minute call to finalize the TPS numbers — Connor, please propose 2x slots.

Best,
Anika
Procurement Lead | LevelUp AI

---
Thread summary: MAP milestones tied to pricing slab options (Option 1 conservative vs Option 2 incentivized), attachments include LevelUp-MAP-v3.pdf and SOW-draft.docx; next action: Redwood to produce formatted acceptance checklist and a short commercial term sheet reflecting Option 2 and renewal uplift language.
